impact.affected_asset: FLAG value inserted by the privileged bot as flag.txt.
impact.attacker_capability: Execute attacker-controlled JavaScript on the shim origin later used by the privileged bot's flag frame and read that frame's document text.
impact.security_effect: Cross-frame plaintext flag disclosure across the intended renderer isolation boundary.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker-controlled page uses the application's share-message interface to submit a non-cached file and manipulate iframe navigation while the privileged browser later visits the attacker URL.

The load listener remains active until a Reloading iframe message; an additional iframe load can cause a second postMessage carrying body and salt after the file has rendered. Deliberately slowing the application process permits that event ordering.

The leaked non-cached salt exposes base36-encoded Math.random outputs. The documented exploit predicts a future salt, then causes a cached attacker payload and the later flag rendering to use the same hash-derived shim origin.

JavaScript from the attacker payload reads the plaintext content of the same-origin flag iframe and sends a value containing CTF{ to the exploit server endpoint; the bot adds the flag as a non-cached text Blob before visiting the attacker page.

failure.operation: Derivation and reuse of an identical hash-based shim origin from an attacker-predicted renderer salt

primary_invariant.kind: per-renderer origin isolation and navigation-bound secret delivery
primary_invariant.statement: Distinct untrusted renderer instances must not obtain the same hash-derived secure origin, and a renderer salt must be delivered only to the intended frame navigation.
primary_invariant.violated_because: A navigation/onload race leaks a Math.random-derived salt; predicted future salts can be selected for a cached attacker payload so its shim origin coincides with the later non-cached flag renderer.

quality.review_notes: Official challenge narrative, source, exploit, and helper support the compound mechanism. The provided exploit includes retry-oriented timing constants and solution notes indicate repeated attempts, so no deterministic execution claim is made. No corrective patch is supplied; remediation is invariant-derived rather than patch-verified.

remediation.invariant_restored: Each renderer instance receives an unguessable, non-reusable origin input, and delivery of body/salt is rejected once the intended navigation identity changes.

target.component: SafeContentFrame renderer and privileged browser workflow
